builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
summary: STARK replaces flat episodic memory stores and retrieval-time episodic traversal with a dual-graph memory: an episodic graph of temporally, causally, and semantically linked events, plus an insight graph of LLM-extracted behavioral signals connected by the events that support them, with event-as-edge relational embeddings enabling cross-user transfer for cold-start users. It costs an LLM call per interaction for insight extraction and scoring, ongoing graph construction and maintenance, an embedding projection for transfer, and added system complexity relative to standard RAG-over-logs memory. It can fail through noisy or incorrect insight extraction that compounds as events accumulate, through embedding- or LLM-judge-based evaluation gains not transferring to the reader's domain, and through privacy or correctness risks when cross-user transfer infers insights for users with little data.
rationale: The dual-graph design is implementable on a single GPU with API-based LLM extraction and claims quality gains, but the reader must validate that the extra extraction and graph-maintenance cost pays off on their own interaction data before production adoption.
technique: Dual-graph long-term agent memory with event-as-edge insights

It costs an LLM call per interaction for insight extraction and scoring, ongoing graph construction and maintenance, an embedding projection for transfer, and added system complexity relative to standard RAG-over-logs memory. It can fail through noisy or incorrect insight extraction that compounds as events accumulate, through embedding- or LLM-judge-based evaluation gains not transferring to the reader's domain, and through privacy or correctness risks when cross-user transfer infers insights for users with little data.

+1.48 judge score on LongMemEval information extraction and +0.93 on LoCoMo open-domain QA over prior SOTA; cross-user transfer adds +0.7 open-ended judge score and +3 ROUGE-L on LongLaMP at 5% graph sparsity.
